S06c: the run manager (codeagent/run_manager.py) -- what makes the run row (S06a) and
the encrypted buffer (S06b) behave as one run.

Everything runs against in-memory twins behind the real interfaces (see
tests/unit/run_manager_testkit.py): the run store, the sweep read, the Redis buffer and
eo/run_guard's Redis, all on one clock, so an idle expiry or the 24 h cap is crossed
without sleeping. The protocol/v1 validation is the REAL one (the same validator the
socket uses). The SQL of the sweep read and the end-to-end behaviour against Postgres are
in tests/integration/test_run_manager_pg.py.

What is pinned:
  * start: the payload is validated first (nothing is written for a bad one, and the
    error never quotes it); the row and the buffer are created together; a buffer that
    cannot be created leaves no `created` zombie; a missing secret is caught before the
    row is written; the parallel-run cap and id collisions leave no buffer behind;
  * the cleanup rule: completed / failed / expired / cancelled leave NOTHING in Redis
    (no buffer key, no run_guard rail); the paused states keep the buffer; two racing
    ends have exactly one winner;
  * cancel: the run_guard flag is set before the row moves, only for the owner's open
    run, it survives a store outage (the user's intent), and nothing is left behind;

S14e: the `run.resume` handler (codeagent/run_handlers.py) and the whole path end to end.

Same setup as the S14c and S14d tests: in-memory twins behind the real interfaces (run store,
encrypted Redis buffer, run_guard's Redis; run_manager_testkit.World), the REAL protocol/v1
validator, a stand-in connection for the unit tests, and S04's real endpoint (codeagent_testkit.Rig)
with the real MessageRouter for the socket tests.

Maps to the work package ("What" 3 run.resume, and "Done when"):
  * the ownership guard first: another device's or user's run, a missing run, an ended run are
    all the same run_not_found, and nothing is changed, bound or sent for them ... test_resume_guard_*
  * run_manager.resume_run, then the events the device missed are re-delivered verbatim, in order,
    and not stored again; then the run is announced `running` (reason resumed) ..... test_resume_replays_*
  * the on_resume hooks run after that, outside the run's lock ........................ test_resume_hooks_*
  * a run that was never paused is reattached as it is; paused_budget stays paused ... test_resume_reattach_*
  * a rebuilt buffer (the server's copy expired and the device sent its state) ........ test_resume_rebuilt_*
  * every failure leaves the run where the device can try again ........................ test_resume_failure_*
  * resumes and live events do not interleave ......................................... test_resume_concurrent_*
  * no content in the log ........................

Patch S05 -- tests for backend/codeagent/adapters/toolcalls.py, the tolerant tool-call parser ported from
MiniLocker (decision D12: copy, never import from the `draft` repo).

Two parts:

  1. MiniLocker's own tests, ported with only two mechanical changes: the import of the parser now points at
     the ported module, and the `TOOLS` fixture that MiniLocker took from `minilocker.agent.loop` is written
     out below (same five tools, same schemas) because that module is not part of this repo. Every test body is
     unchanged. Where the port and a test disagreed the port was adjusted, never the test (build plan 11.6, rule 2).
  2. "M2C additions" at the bottom: the same malformed-argument and refusal rules, exercised against the real
     P00 tool schemas (protocol/v1/tools/*.json), because those are the tools M2C actually offers.

Pure: no network, no sockets, no Docker.

What is pinned here is the JOINING: which parts the process loop is made of, what install() registers on S14's run

S04 (device socket, WS /v1/code/device): the handshake, authentication for
the life of the connection, validation, limits, and the protocol fixtures.

The real endpoint (codeagent/ws.py), the real registry (codeagent/connections.py),
the real eo/devices.py logic and the real protocol/v1 schemas run here; only the
device table is faked (devices_testkit.FakeStore, via codeagent_testkit.WsFakeStore).
Every frame the server sends is also validated against protocol/v1, strictly, so
the server cannot drift from the contract it is built against.

Maps to the work package's "Done when":
  * tests replay the protocol fixtures against a fake device ..... test_replay_fixture_*
  * an unknown, malformed or revoked credential is refused ........ test_unknown_*, test_malformed_*,
                                                                    test_revoked_credential_*
  * a device revoked while connected is disconnected at the next
    re-check ...................................................... test_device_revoked_while_connected_*
  * messages that fail schema validation get invalid_message and
    do not crash the socket ...................................... test_invalid_*, test_every_invalid_example_*

S04: what the device socket does when it cannot do its job, and how it is mounted.

Deliberately NOT guarded by pytest.importorskip("jsonschema"): the socket validates
every message against protocol/v1 with jsonschema (loaded lazily, see codeagent/ws.py
"Runtime needs"), and the promise is that when that -- or the protocol/ directory,
which the backend image does not contain today -- is unavailable, the server still
starts, the rest of the app is unaffected, and the device socket REFUSES connections
instead of accepting messages it cannot check. These tests do not need jsonschema.
